presentation.summary: A deliberately conservative owner-only comparison point: 10 valid consecutive standard push-ups under the exact governed protocol. The number is an AGAS engineering judgment, not a textbook norm and not a statement authored by the athlete.

authority_basis.numeric_value_explanation: The value 10 was selected by AGAS engineering as a provisional whole-number minimum for repeated performance on this exact test. It was not extracted from ACSM's sex-specific reference table.
authority_basis.operational_use_explanation: Using 10 repetitions as an owner-alpha competency floor is an accountable, replaceable product judgment. Ratification would adopt that narrow use without converting it into a scientific finding.

governs: Whether a current matching standard-push-up estimate is below, meets, or exceeds this provisional owner-alpha floor.
Whether that comparison may enter a separately reviewed planning context for upper-body muscular endurance.
does_not_establish: A published population norm, fitness grade, sex-based category, or health threshold.
Medical safety, pain-free readiness, pressing strength, or total-body athleticism.
A push-up exercise prescription, number of sets, training intensity, session, or progression rule.
Applicability to another athlete, age band, push-up variation, or movement standard.
unresolved_limitations: No study or textbook table validates 10 standard push-ups as a minimum useful athletic competency.
The owner has not yet supplied a personal result under the governed protocol, so longitudinal calibration is not available.
A self-counted maximum can vary with technique, familiarization, fatigue, and motivation.
The floor should be reviewed after initial measurement and training-response history exist.

evidence.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 12th edition
evidence.population: Apparently healthy adults addressed by the guideline; the source's reference categories are age- and sex-stratified.
evidence.finding: The source supports the standardized maximum-consecutive-push-up protocol and its narrow upper-body muscular-endurance construct; it does not support the AGAS value of 10.
limitations: The table uses standard push-ups for males and modified knee push-ups for females, so its rows are not directly comparable.
The supporting source establishes the protocol and construct, not this numeric floor.
evidence.conflict_disclosure: No protocol-specific conflict disclosure was identified in the inspected textbook pages; AGAS did not independently audit the cited primary studies.

source.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
provenance_notes: The owner supplied a local copy for review; the PDF itself is not stored in AGAS.
The NLM Catalog record confirms the editors, edition, publisher, and EPUB ISBN 9781975219246.
The protocol statement was checked against Chapter 3, PDF pages 244-245, including Box 3.10.
Table 3.11 was inspected but its sex-specific categories are not activated by this release.

claim.claim: ACSM's 12th-edition guideline supports a standardized maximum-consecutive-push-up protocol and its narrow upper-body muscular-endurance construct, but does not establish a sex-neutral universal threshold or the AGAS value of 10 repetitions.
claim.population: Apparently healthy adults addressed by the guideline; the accompanying reference categories are age- and sex-stratified and do not define one universal population.
claim.intervention: Maximum consecutive push-up field test performed with the Box 3.10 technique.
claim.comparator: No comparator is required for the direct repetition-count observation.
claim.outcome: Maximum consecutive repetitions completed without rest while technique is retained.
claim.study_design: Professional guideline and textbook synthesis citing primary references 166-168
claim.effect_direction: A larger valid repetition count represents greater performance on this exact test.
claim.uncertainty: The source provides a protocol and descriptive reference categories; it does not establish an AGAS competency floor, exercise prescription, or total-body fitness inference.
limitations: Push-up results are specific to the exact movement, range of motion, pace, and stopping rules.
Table 3.11 uses standard push-ups for males and modified knee push-ups for females, so its rows are not directly comparable.
The textbook does not reproduce subgroup sampling details for the reference table.
Self-counted technique has not been independently validated by this release.
claim.applicability_notes: The no-equipment field protocol is practical for an adult recreationally trained athlete, but only within-person tracking of the standard version is authorized.
claim.reviewer: Codex floor-support evidence synthesis candidate; authority pending

evidence_review_content.source_verification_rationale: The construct statement, consecutive-without-rest score, technique criteria, stopping rule, sex-specific protocol difference, and normative limitation were checked against Chapter 3, Box 3.10 and Table 3.11 on PDF pages 244-245.
evidence_review_content.extraction_rationale: The claim retains only the source-supported test construct and procedure. It does not import an age/sex category, percentile, fitness grade, or training dose.
evidence_review_content.evidence_strength_rationale: Low reflects use of a textbook synthesis for a narrow protocol claim without independent appraisal of its cited primary validation studies.
evidence_review_content.applicability_rationale: Moderate reflects a practical no-equipment adult field test while limiting interpretation to repeat performance on the exact standard version.
evidence_review_content.uncertainty: Self-counting, technique drift, familiarization, fatigue, and day-to-day variation may materially affect the result.
evidence_review_content.conflict_disclosure: No protocol-specific conflict disclosure was identified in the inspected textbook pages; this is not a claim that the cited primary studies had none.

authority.statement: For the owner-alpha athlete only, treat 10 valid consecutive standard push-ups under the exact governed protocol as a provisional minimum useful repeat-performance floor.
authority.population: Owner-only alpha; age 30 to 39; recreationally trained adult doing physical work.
authority.rationale: Ten is a deliberately conservative whole-number threshold that distinguishes an inability to sustain a short series of valid repetitions from capacity suitable for maintenance review. The number is an engineering judgment, not a source-derived norm.
authority.applicability_notes: Use only with a current estimate from the exact governed standard-push-up protocol. Review after personal baseline and response history exist.
authority.uncertainty: No scientific source validates 10 repetitions as a minimum useful athletic competency, and the first personal result may show that this floor is too low or otherwise unhelpful.
limitations: This threshold has no population-validity claim.
It cannot establish medical safety, pressing strength, total-body fitness, or an exercise dose.
It may be cleared easily by the owner and therefore yield maintenance rather than development.
Personal longitudinal calibration should replace it when enough observations exist.
authority.authored_by: AGAS engineering candidate prepared by Codex
authority.qualification_context: System engineering synthesis; not user-authored and not a claim of a licensed clinical or strength credential. A planning reviewer must explicitly adopt the exact judgment before operational use.

authority_review_content.attestation: I adopt this exact owner-alpha product judgment for narrow planning use and understand that the value 10 is not a scientific finding, population norm, safety clearance, or exercise prescription.
authority_review_content.uncertainty: Approval does not establish external validity; replace or withdraw this authority when personal calibration or better applicable evidence supports a different decision.

floor.population: Owner-only alpha; age 30 to 39; exact governed standard-push-up protocol.
floor.applicability_notes: Compare only with a current estimate from the matching governed protocol. Use the result as one planning input; never as diagnosis, safety clearance, or a universal fitness judgment.
floor.uncertainty: The threshold is an explicit AGAS engineering judgment with supporting protocol evidence but no numeric scientific validation. It is provisional and replaceable after personal calibration.

floor_review_content.applicability_rationale: Approve only for the owner-alpha athlete, ages 30 to 39, after a current estimate from the exact standard-push-up protocol. The comparison may inform development or maintenance but is not a medical or safety decision.
floor_review_content.uncertainty: The protocol construct is source-supported; the number 10 is not. Approval adopts the separate reviewed engineering authority and requires later personal calibration.

release.release_rationale: Provide one honest, owner-relevant floor so the governed standard-push-up estimate can enter planning without inferring sex or disguising a product judgment as a textbook result.
release.release_uncertainty: Ratification authorizes only this owner-alpha comparison. It creates no diagnosis, universal norm, adaptation priority, workout, exercise dose, session, or progression.
